title: Lexicon soft-launch capacity guardrails for new model activation
summary: Short note with pragmatic guardrails and a simulation snapshot for a controlled soft-launch of 'lexicon-13b-improved'. Focused on GPU headroom per region, expected KV cache growth, warmup strategy, admission controls, and quick rollback triggers. Purpose: give SRE and infra oncall a checklist and parameterized configs to graduate from internal beta to a public canary while avoiding cache saturation and cross-region tail latency spikes.
objectives: Quantify additional KV cache footprint and eviction pressure for lexicon-13b under three workload mixes
Define per-region safe headroom thresholds and burst allowances for the first 48 hours
Prescribe autoscaler and admission-control settings to maintain 99th percentile latency SLOs
List monitoring keys and automated rollback triggers for confidence during soft-launch
assumptions: Baseline fleet as of 2026-02: eu-west-1=120 GPUs, us-west-2=200 GPUs, us-east-1=220 GPUs, ap-southeast-1=60 GPUs
Current KV cache occupancy average (all existing models) across fleet: 72% of usable pool
Lexicon-13b-improved average request context length: 1.2k tokens, median 512 tokens
Warmup prefetch per new session will create ~28KB KV entries per user session; cold-start sessions increase transient cache pressure
Adoption scenario A/B/C described in scenarios table (see below)
scenarios:
Scenario | Traffic ramp | Active users (global) | % requests that hit lexicon
A - conservative | +10% over baseline | 8k active | 15%
B - expected | +30% over baseline | 25k active | 40%
C - aggressive | +75% over baseline | 70k active | 65%
(Assumes rollout to 3 regions in parallel: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1)
simulation_results:
We ran a 48h synthetic shadow-simulation using sampled request traces with lexicon KV-profile applied. Key outputs:
- Scenario A: peak KV occupancy increase +6% absolute (to ~78%), average GPU utilization bump +4ppt, no region exceeded soft-threshold.
- Scenario B: peak KV occupancy increase +18% absolute (to ~90%), eu-west-1 exceeded soft-threshold for 3 discrete 7-minute windows, increased eviction churn observed. Estimated token-cost delta ~+12% for hosted.
- Scenario C: KV occupancy hit >98% in ap-southeast-1 simulation (local cluster had less headroom), eviction cascades caused 95th pct latency degradation ~+210ms. GPU saturation windows observed in US regions for sustained 20-40 minute periods.
Notes: simulations assume current autoscaler settings (scale delta 10 GPUs/min, cooldown 5m) and no pre-warming of KV. Warmup shadowing reduced cold-penalty by ~35% in traces where present.
recommended_autoscaler_config: Immediate: temporarily raise reserved headroom per region by +8% of baseline GPU pool for first 72h of rollout (config flag: rollout_reserve_pct=8)
Autoscaler tuning: decrease scale cooldown to 90s for lexicon-tagged queues, increase max-scale-step to 30 GPUs for emergency spikes
Admission control: per-account QPS throttle for lexicon endpoints (default 10 QPS, canary cohort exceptions for partners)
KV pre-warm: enable seeded KV warmup for 20% of expected canary users using synthetic sessions to populate common prefixes
Prefer local serving affinity: avoid cross-region spillover by setting routing policy to prefer same-region capacity unless latency SLO violated
monitoring_and_rollbacks:
Monitoring signals to surface in the first 72 hours: KV eviction rate, KV occupancy (90/95/99 pct), GPU slot queue length, P95/P99 token latency, model-specific error-rate, cross-region spillover fraction. Automated rollback triggers (auto-trigger a staged rollback to previous model variant OR limit traffic to 10%):
- KV eviction rate > 3x baseline sustained for 10m
- Region KV occupancy > 95% for 5m
- P99 token latency increase > 200ms correlated with lexicon traffic for 3 consecutive 5m windows
- Error rate jump > 2% absolute and > 3x relative to baseline
Manual override: SRE oncall or product PM can trigger rollback immediately. All triggers should open a dedicated incident channel with triage checklist linked.
estimated_cost_delta: First 7 days: conservative scenario +3-6% infra token/GPU spend due to warmup and slightly increased utilization. Expected scenario +9-15% driven by KV eviction penalties and additional GPU-hours. Aggressive scenario could double short-term marginal costs in hotspot regions until autoscaler and routing mitigations engage. Rough numbers: expected scenario adds ~0.18 GPU-hours per active lexicon user per day aggregated (global). Recommend finance ops review if projected monthly delta > $75k.
risk_matrix:
Risk: KV pool saturation -> Impact: high -> Likelihood: medium (without mitigations) -> Mitigation: seeded warmup, reserve headroom, aggressive admission control
Risk: cross-region spillover -> Impact: medium-high -> Likelihood: medium -> Mitigation: prefer-region routing + per-region canary thresholds
Risk: longer tail latencies -> Impact: high -> Likelihood: low-medium -> Mitigation: tighten alerts on P99, fast rollback triggers, model variant fallback
Risk: cost overrun -> Impact: medium -> Likelihood: medium -> Mitigation: timeboxed budget limit and daily spend report to finance/growth
rollback_triggers: P99 token latency increase > 200ms correlated with lexicon traffic 3x windows
Unplanned autoscaler thrash (scale up/down cycles > 6 in 30m)
next_steps: Schedule war room runbook review with SRE and serving-runtime (target: 2026-03-08)
Create a canary cohort of 5 partners and internal beta users to seed pre-warm flows
Deploy KV pre-warm job and validate steady-state eviction metrics in staging cluster
Apply temporary autoscaler tuning flags in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 and monitor for 24h
Prepare finance alert for daily spend > $12k incremental during soft-launch
checklist: Confirm rollout_reserve_pct flag set in infra config
KV pre-warm job scheduled and validated in staging
Alerting runbook published and linked in incident channel
Canary cohort invited and traffic split configured (default 5% of test traffic)
SRE oncall rotation aware and paged during first 72 hours
